QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_42

question.text: Under Regulation 20 AIF Regulations, if the Sponsor of Nilgiri AIF is a LISTED company, what constitutes 'control'?

answer.text: Only direct shareholding of 50% or more.
The right to appoint majority of the directors, or to control the management or policy decisions — exercisable by person(s) acting individually or in concert, directly or indirectly.
Any voting-rights arrangement is automatically excluded from 'control'.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per AIF Regulations Chapter 12 definition: For a listed/unlisted company Sponsor/Manager, 'control' includes the right to appoint majority of the directors or to control the management or policy decisions exercisable by person(s) acting individually or in concert, directly or indirectly, including by virtue of shareholding / management rights / shareholders' agreements / voting agreements, etc. **The Trap:** 50% is a bright-line test more appropriate to non-company sponsors. Options C and D contradict the express definition, which is broad and captures indirect/voting arrangements. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C identical definition. SAST Regulations use similar-but-distinct 'control' for takeover purposes (XXI-B / VIII may test SAST control). **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In change-of-control diligence, trace 'acting in concert' carefully — promoter family offices and their overseas vehicles often create aggregated control that is missed in a single-entity SPA review.
